definition: P32 ward-level evidence-state closures for the three health-facility indicators (IND-HEALTH-FACILITY-COUNT, IND-HEALTH-FACILITY-STOCK, IND-INPATIENT-SERVICE-AVAILABILITY) that PR #243 investigated and closed official_unavailable at constituency level. This file does not cover IND-HEALTH-FACILITY-DENSITY, which already has its own, separately-resolved ward-level closure inside data/completeness/local-54-slot-ledger.json from P24/P28A. These three indicators carry no ward slot in the P18 public-taxonomy (data/indicators/seed/placeholder-taxonomy.json) -- they surface only through the raw canonical indicator registry and the P26-P32 local-54 framework -- so a genuinely researched, specifically-cited ward closure for them cannot live in the shared data/completeness/evidence-states.json without risking that file's P18-specific, exact-count reconciliation (scripts/completeness/validate-slot-ledger.mjs) or a merge conflict with other P32 batches concurrently adding their own entries there. This file is consumed only by scripts/p29/build-local-54-slot-ledger.mjs, exactly like data/completeness/evidence-states.json, but scoped to indicators/levels the older P18 taxonomy never covers. Each entry reflects a genuine, fresh 2026-09-19 re-check (live KMHFR/opendata.go.ke reachability tests, and re-fetched/byte-compared source PDFs) rather than a mechanical extension of the constituency-level finding, per this project's anti-fabrication rule -- no parent-level (county or constituency) value is ever spatially allocated down into ward cells.

states.period_label: 2023 Kenya Health Facility Census (14-29 August 2023) · current 1,450-ward boundary
states.source: Kenya Master Health Facility Registry (KMHFR); Ministry of Health -- Kenya Health Facility Census Report September 2023
states.refresh_trigger: Replace this closure when KMHFR (or another authoritative Ministry of Health facility registry) becomes reachable with per-facility ward tagging exposed via a working portal/API/export, or when the Ministry publishes a facility-count table below county for the 2023 census (or a successor census) covering the current 1,450-ward boundary.
states.reason: PR #243's constituency-level closure (contract_id P31-HEALTH-FACILITY-COUNT-CONSTITUENCY-UNAVAILABLE-2026-09-18, data/completeness/evidence-states.json) found KMHFR's public facility portal (https://kmhfr.health.go.ke/public/facilities) and its apex host (https://kmhfr.health.go.ke/) unreachable, opendata.go.ke likewise unreachable, and the published "Kenya Health Facility Census Report September 2023" Table 2 ("County Summary; Facilities Targeted Over Facilities Assessed, Closed & Denied Access", p.5) tabulating exactly 47 county rows and no finer geography. This P32 ward-level review re-ran that verification fresh rather than mechanically extending it, because access to a live registry could plausibly change day to day: a fresh live HTTPS check on 2026-09-19 again found kmhfr.health.go.ke/public/facilities and the KMHFR apex host (kmhfr.health.go.ke) unreachable -- both connection attempts timed out after 20 seconds with no TCP handshake completing, the identical failure signature recorded on 2026-09-18 (this indicator's own constituency check), 2026-09-16 (P28A) and the original P24 check -- and opendata.go.ke was re-tested and is likewise still unreachable (20-second timeout, no handshake). In the same test run, health.go.ke's own apex domain again responded normally (HTTP 200, sub-1-second latency), confirming this remains a targeted, persistent failure of the KMHFR host specifically, not a general government-domain or network outage. The published census report was re-fetched as a fallback check: both mirrors (health.go.ke and repository.familyhealth.go.ke) remain reachable (HTTP 200), and the health.go.ke mirror's HTTP headers show it is byte-identical to the copy already reviewed -- Content-Length 6,307,134 bytes and Last-Modified Mon, 08 Jan 2024, unchanged since the original review -- so its Table 2 (47 county rows, no finer geography) is confirmed unchanged rather than merely assumed unchanged. The underlying barrier this indicator faces is access to KMHFR/the census microdata, not the geography level itself: a ward is a strict subdivision of a constituency, so if the live registry cannot be reached to tabulate 290 constituency-level facility counts, it equally cannot be reached to tabulate 1,450 ward-level facility counts, and if the one published documentary fallback table stops at county with no finer geography at all, it provides no ward row either. Kenya's administrative sub-counties and wards are in any case not an authoritative match to electoral wards without a verified crosswalk (docs/LOCAL-INDICATOR-CASCADE-CONTRACT.md), so even a hypothetical sub-county table would not by itself resolve this cell. Both the live-registry numerator source and its only published documentary fallback remain genuinely blocked at ward level today, for the same reasons already governing the constituency-level closure.

states.period_label: Kenya Health Facility Census, facilities targeted from the KMHFL as at 1 August 2023 · current 1,450-ward boundary
states.source: Ministry of Health -- Kenya Health Facility Census Report September 2023
states.refresh_trigger: Replace this closure when the Ministry publishes a facilities-targeted/KMHFL-derived count below county for the current 1,450-ward boundary, or when KMHFR becomes reachable with a queryable ward field so the underlying KMHFL list can itself be tabulated by ward.
states.reason: PR #243's constituency-level closure (contract_id P31-HEALTH-FACILITY-STOCK-CONSTITUENCY-UNAVAILABLE-2026-09-18, data/completeness/evidence-states.json) found the Kenya Health Facility Census Report September 2023's Table 2 ("County Summary; Facilities Targeted Over Facilities Assessed, Closed & Denied Access", p.5) -- the source of this indicator's "Target Facilities" figures, drawn from the Kenya Master Health Facility List (KMHFL) as at 1 August 2023 -- to be county-only (47 rows), and the KMHFL's own maintaining registry, KMHFR, unreachable. This P32 ward-level review re-ran that verification fresh rather than mechanically extending it: a fresh live HTTPS check on 2026-09-19 again found kmhfr.health.go.ke/public/facilities and the KMHFR apex host unreachable -- both connection attempts timed out after 20 seconds with no TCP handshake completing, the identical failure signature recorded on 2026-09-18, 2026-09-16 (P28A) and the original P24 check -- while health.go.ke's own apex domain again responded normally (HTTP 200), confirming this remains a targeted, persistent KMHFR-host failure, not a general outage. Both published mirrors of the census report (health.go.ke and repository.familyhealth.go.ke) were re-fetched and remain reachable (HTTP 200); the health.go.ke mirror's HTTP headers show it is byte-identical to the copy already reviewed -- Content-Length 6,307,134 bytes and Last-Modified Mon, 08 Jan 2024, unchanged -- so Table 2's county-only structure is confirmed unchanged, not merely assumed unchanged. No official geocoded/constituency- or ward-tagged KMHFL export was found on the Humanitarian Data Exchange or elsewhere beyond the already-identified 2017 HDX snapshot (no coordinates, predates the 2023 census) -- that finding does not change with geography level, since it concerns whether any such export exists at all. The underlying barrier is access to the KMHFL/KMHFR source, not the geography level: since a ward is a strict subdivision of a constituency, the same registry-access failure and the same county-only published fallback that block a 290-constituency tabulation equally block a 1,450-ward tabulation. This cell remains genuinely blocked at both its documentary and registry sources at ward level today, for the same reasons already governing the constituency-level closure.

states.period_label: SARA facility survey (fieldwork reflected in the report dated 21 October 2025, published to health.go.ke June 2026) · Table 18, county-level only
states.source: Ministry of Health -- Service Availability and Readiness Assessment (SARA), Table 18
states.refresh_trigger: Replace this closure if a future SARA cycle publishes Table 18 (or an equivalent inpatient-service-availability table) disaggregated below county with sampling weights calibrated to support a defensible ward (or exact-crosswalk sub-county) estimate.
states.reason: PR #243's constituency-level closure (contract_id P31-INPATIENT-SERVICE-AVAILABILITY-CONSTITUENCY-UNAVAILABLE-2026-09-18, data/completeness/evidence-states.json) found the Ministry of Health's Service Availability and Readiness Assessment (SARA) report's Table 18 ("Percentage of facilities with Inpatient services", p.61) to be county-only across every one of the report's 434 pages, and -- independently of the publication gap -- the report's own Study Limitations section (2.11, p.19) states that its facility-sample "sampling weights ... [were] applied to produce both national and county-level estimates" only. That calibration limitation is a statistical-design fact about the survey's sample and weighting scheme -- comparable to a fixed survey domain -- so it constrains what estimates the dataset can defensibly support regardless of which geography level (constituency or ward) is being asked for; it does not get weaker or stronger as the target geography shrinks from 290 constituencies to 1,450 wards. This P32 ward-level review re-verified rather than assumed this still holds: the SARA report was re-fetched fresh on 2026-09-19 from its published URL (https://health.go.ke/sites/default/files/2026-06/Main%20Report%20-%20SARA%2021.10.2025.pdf) and remains reachable (HTTP 200); its HTTP headers show it is byte-identical to the copy already fully text-searched for PR #243 -- Content-Length 19,611,538 bytes (19.6MB, matching the prior review) and Last-Modified Fri, 05 Jun 2026, unchanged -- confirming Table 18's county-only structure and the Study Limitations section's calibration statement are unchanged, not merely assumed unchanged, and that no newer SARA edition with finer geography has superseded it. Since the survey's own sampling weights are calibrated only for national and county estimates, no ward-level (nor constituency-level) estimate can be produced defensibly from this dataset without re-weighting work outside the scope of the published survey -- exactly the reasoning that closed this indicator at constituency level, applying identically and without modification to wards. Both the publication and the underlying survey design independently confirm this indicator cannot be resolved below county from SARA today, at ward level exactly as at constituency level.
